description:
Found by defk-52v.3 (examples/lz4_snappy_decode.exs). Inside an Enum.reduce_while (or for reduce:) body, `if done, do: {:halt, {out, s}}, else: (out = put1(out, i); {:cont, {out, s}})` where put1/2 is a kernel that writes out[i] and returns out: the inlined callee copies `out` before its write on EVERY iteration (report: "copy: out is copied before this write: another binding still sees its buffer"), and every copy lives until the kernel returns. Time and memory are quadratic in the loop length. Writing `out[i] = 1` directly in the same branch does not copy, and hoisting the call out of the branch (`out = put1(out, i)` first, then `if done, do: {:halt, ...}, else: {:cont, ...}`) does not copy either.

Reproduction (Mix.install script):

    defk put1(out :: [u8], i :: i64) :: [u8] do
      out[i] = 1
      out
    end

    defk fill(n :: i64) :: i64 do
      out = alloc(u8, n)
      {out, s} =
        Enum.reduce_while(0..(n - 1)//1, {out, 0}, fn i, {out, s} ->
          if i == n - 1 do
            {:halt, {out, s + out[0]}}
          else
            out = put1(out, i)
            {:cont, {out, s}}
          end
        end)
      s + out[1]
    end

Measured: n = 1k 92 us, 10k 12 ms, 40k 202 ms (hoisted: 1, 4, 7 us); 40k holds ~1.6 GB of copies. In the LZ4/Snappy decoder (copy helper per element, 4 MB output) the BEAM was SIGKILLed (exit 137, out of memory): a kernel took the node down, which the runtime contract says it must not.

Likely cause: the "read after the write" test for an inlined callee's array parameter sees the caller's `out` read by name in the other branch of the enclosing if (or in the next iteration through the accumulator), although the caller rebinds `out` to the result. The direct-write path already handles this case.

Done when: the reproduction copies nothing (fast-path report has no copy note for fill/1, timing linear), a test covers a helper call in one branch with a read in the other, and docs/language.md Copies says how a helper call in a branch behaves. Separately consider a bound on the memory a kernel's copies may hold (a copy in a loop that keeps every buffer until return can exhaust memory).
title: [BUG] A helper kernel that writes and returns an array, called in one branch of a loop body whose other branch reads the array, copies the whole array every iteration and keeps every copy
